findings.reason: the calibration column is still an open done-when item, and naming the existing owner would either route it through the shipped loop or force a stated reason to fork it.
findings.text: §3 adds a per-section authored-vs-measured calibration column whose "calibration table is fed by every landing", but the plan names no existing mechanism for it and never mentions `reckon/calibration.py`, `calibrate_plan_estimates`/`calibrate_agent_speeds`, or the shipped `effort-calibration` plan, so the reviewer cannot tell whether the same loop is being rebuilt

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend `reckon/calibration.py` to section granularity (reusing `_eligible_runs`' duration-provenance and exclusion rules) rather than add a parallel calibration reader.
findings.text: `calibrate_plan_estimates` already owns the authored-versus-measured effort feedback loop (fed by recorded runs, with `effort_calibrated` surfaced per plan in `reckon/roadmap.py:463`), so §3's section-granular table is a second owner of one calibration concept

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the two new entry points hide real work behind small interfaces: `resolve_section_routing` (record read + attempt count + one-way raise + backend resolution) and `derive_impl_from_sections` (ratio plus the coverage rule) each expose one function for behaviour spread across reads, a join and a policy.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 proposes a "calibration table fed by every landing" comparing authored against measured effort, which forks the loop that `reckon/calibration.py` already owns at plan granularity.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the DAG/section-ref machinery (depends_on, gated_sections, parse_plan_ref) and cites it in §6, but never cites the shipped effort/calibration subsystem (`reckon/calibration.py`, the `effort-calibration` plan) that §3's calibration column re-creates at section granularity.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan's new layers compose existing mechanisms rather than forwarding to them: §5 wraps `resolve_role` *and* adds the raise, §1 extends the existing `plan-section-declarations` store rather than forking it, and §7 collapses three readers onto one predicate (`unwired_plan_finding`) instead of adding a parallel one.
